subject: reasoning
question: Ishan starts from Point Y and drives 21 km towards the north. He then takes a left turn, drives 42 km, turns left and drives 41 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 17 km. He takes a right turn, drives 59 km. He then turns right, drives 18 km, turns right and drives 39 km to stop at Point Z. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point Y again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only unless specified.)
solution:
Given:

Ishan starts from Point Y and drives 21 km towards the north.

He then takes a left turn, drives 42 km, turns left and drives 41 km.

He then takes a right turn and drives 17 km.

He takes a right turn, drives 59 km.

He then turns right, drives 18 km, turns right and drives 39 km to stop at Point Z. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a3b1aeafedf61cc8005ca408e528364a6a47223f3e07d4adf67d8f6da98add7a.png] 

Thus, Ishan should drive 41 km (42 km + 17 km - 18 km) in the east direction in order to reach Point Y again.​

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.
